exposure: smoking status (current, recent former, remote former)
cohort: The study included 136,018 eligible respondents aged 45 years or older from the 2019 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) survey.
finding: There was a graded association between smoking and subjective cognitive decline (SCD), with current smokers having the highest prevalence of SCD, followed by recent former smokers, and then remote former smokers, all compared to never smokers.
